name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: US hit Qeshm, Iran fired on Kuwait 18 Nov
summary: US struck Qeshm and Iran fired drones at Kuwait and Bahrain on 18 Nov; Qatar says talks remain the best route
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched drones at a US radar at Bahrain's Isa air base on 17 Nov; the US military said they were intercepted (Al Jazeera). On 18 Nov a US strike hit a missile launch site on Qeshm Island, and Kuwait and Bahrain said they intercepted Iranian aerial attacks; on 19 Nov President Trump said he was in contact with Iranian representatives, and mediator Qatar said on 20 Nov that negotiations remain the best route (Gulf News). Peace talks have stalled (New York Times). Active strikes between states keep the Alert.
for_you: British nationals in the Gulf should follow FCDO travel advice for each country, which can change at short notice. Flights across the region may be disrupted or rerouted.
rubric_hit: Alert: active strikes between states (US strike on Qeshm; Iranian drone attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain, 17–18 Nov)

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Bahrain thwarts drone attack; Iran claims targeting US radar
Gulf News — Riyadh skyscraper damaged, tanker hit near Oman as Trump weighs fresh Iran strikes
New York Times via Philadelphia Inquirer — Iran keeps up unrelenting attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
